found.summary:
Most of chunk 7 checks out against the code, Live's data and RoF2: interiors as copies of their dz templates, entering, the exit point, /leaverealestate, house pick-up, the swap's codes, Store All, the latch, layout validation, anchors (437/438, 5329, landing height) and polls.

Statements that are wrong or out of date:
- the crate model: "a child property of its plot". On Live, 16 of 34 placed crates stand in a house or hall, and RoF2 searches the whole plot.
- the zone registration count: about 524, not 272.
- "PEQ has none of them".
- the layout file's fields.
- the poll prompt at zone-in. RoF2 shows it itself, once per vote window, not by 0x7a4d.
- 0x154a is never sent.
- T23's timer.
- the upstream note on 437/438.
- opting another member out of trophies (TRO-1).
- the "verified in game" line.

Main gaps:
1. **High.** A crate placed in a house is refused by Pack, Unpack, Move to Storage and the sale. The crate limit only looks at the destination.
2. **Medium.** A forged swap naming a house stored in the outgoing house's own closet leaves that house's item inside its own property.
3. **Medium.** DOR-17's renumbering left the Guild Lobby's quest script on PEQ's old door ids, and Live's door 1 route into the guild's own guild hall exists nowhere.

There are also low items: no source for anchors, Pack/Unpack skipping houses, anchor messages, the layout load's ids, poll robustness, exit corners, evidence for INT-41, untested interiors, trophy rule 70 and plan text.

The Ghidra outputs are in C:/Onyx/scratch/ghidra/prc2/chunk7*.txt.

gaps.description: The server only finds a crate placed directly in the yard. RoF2 and Live allow it in a house or hall and enforce one crate per plot. With the crate placed in a house (which the server's own rules accept), Pack, Unpack and Move to Storage into the crate get 22. A sale gets code 4 although the client's gate passes it. The crate limit checks only the destination, so a forged commit can put a second crate under a plot, or place a house holding a crate on a plot that already has one.
gaps.evidence:
Live (master/properties.tsv with propertyItems.tsv): 16 of 34 placed moving crates stand in houses (12) or halls (4); none of the 40 crate properties shares a plot with another.

RoF2:
- 0x5b48b0 (rof2PlaceRules3.txt:66-160) climbs to the plot (0x4d6790, types 4/8). It refuses a crate when 0x5b45b0 finds another crate property anywhere below. It also refuses a house holding a crate on a plot that has one.
- The crate Pack and Unpack use (manager +0xa0) comes from the same search (0x5b0140).
- The sell gate searches the plot recursively too: 0x5b47d0, and 0x5b7fa0 via 0x5b7e10(6, plot, ..., 1).
- Sources: prc2/chunk7Decomp1.txt, chunk7Decomp4.txt, chunk7Decomp5.txt.

Code 22's text is 'You must have a moving crate placed in your yard or house for this operation.' Crate items are placeable 142. PLC-30 tested only a yard crate.
gaps.proposedAction:
- Find the plot's crate as RoF2 does (climb to the plot, take the crate property at any depth) for Pack, Unpack, Move to Storage and the sale; answer 22 when it isn't placed.
- On placement, refuse 16 when another crate property exists under the plot, or when a house holding a crate goes onto a plot that has one.
- Rewrite serverPlan.md:582.
- Check the sale on Live: eqstr 81 forbids packing a house that holds the crate into it.
gaps.liveCheck: Place a storage crate inside a house on a plot that holds other items. Press Pack inside the house, then sell the plot, and record what moves, any refusal text, and what the crate holds afterwards.

gaps.description: The swap never checks where the stored house is. Suppose an empty house is stored in the outgoing house's own closet; the closet bars only non-empty houses. A forged 0x21ba naming it places that house in the yard. The move loop then walks the outgoing house's rows as they were before the swap, so it moves the same row into the new house's own property, unplaced. The client is told the swap succeeded, and the house, with anything later put in it, becomes unreachable.
gaps.evidence:
- The stored row is taken from any session property (:1313-1333).
- After updateRow(incoming) (:1388-1402), the loop over view.rowsOf(outgoingHouseId) (:1407-1419) still holds the row's old copy and writes property_id = incomingHouseId, placed 0.
- maySwap offers Swap only on a yard's storage (housingMenus.cpp:120-130), so only a forged request reaches this.
- Rule 32 (resultCodes.md:31) keeps only non-empty houses out of the closet.
gaps.proposedAction: Refuse a swap unless the stored house's row sits in the yard's own storage, as the menu offers it. Leave the incoming row out of the moved rows in any case. Add the case to tests/housingTest.h.

findings.title: `_Guild<rank>` entries never match on a player plot
findings.description: characterRankKey builds the `_Guild<rank>` key only when the subject's stored guild_id is the client's guild. A player plot's guild_id is always 0, so on a player plot, and on its houses and crates, a `_Guild<rank>` entry never matches. An owner may grant their guild through the Manage window's Owner's Clubs. The server treats those guildmates as Everyone: it refuses Enter, menu entries (Move Item, Mail Item, Remove Crate), withdrawals and access edits. setClientView never seeds the plot for them either, so their client gets neither the record nor the list and refuses as well.
findings.evidence:
- **Stored guild:** housingPurchase.cpp:164-168 writes guild_id 0 for a player plot, and activeGuildId (housingAccess.cpp:70-72) reads that column.
- **Client rule:** the client's group computation (permissions.md, 0x4ff250, guild compare at 0x4ff3c6-0x4ff3d2) uses `_Guild<rank>` when the character's guild equals record +0x24.
- **What Peridot sends:** for a player plot, record +0x24 is the owner's current guild (housing.cpp:217-222, REC-9).
- **Live (ACC-3, 2026-10-17):** on Anastrianaa's player plot 117730767, `_Guild1` set to Visitor gave Pariator, leader of her guild, the same menus as the named Visitor under all 28 masks.

findings.title: NO TRADE alternate currency crosses accounts through escrow
findings.description:
Anyone may deposit any escrow currency into any owned plot. Anyone with Withdraw Upkeep (the owner, Trustees, Co-Owners, guild officers) can withdraw any currency, and a sale pays the whole escrow to the seller. Nothing checks NO TRADE.

So a NO TRADE currency (Faycetum, currency 14 on Peridot) can move between accounts in two ways:
- character A deposits it into B's plot, and B withdraws it;
- a Trustee on another account withdraws what the owner deposited.

The transfer path refuses an escrow that holds NO TRADE currency (8081), which shows the design means such currency not to change hands. Serverplan.md:460's 'a deposit only helps the owner' did not consider this case.
findings.evidence:
- **Transfer refusal exists:** housingTransfer.cpp:73-86 refuses NO TRADE escrow with 8081. STT-7: 5 Faycetum (NO TRADE) in an escrow drew 8081 on peridothousing.
- **Strangers deposit on Live:** UPK-8 shows a stranger depositing coin from the plot's Purchase window.
- **The client checks nothing:** RoF2's deposit routine (0x741ee0, decompiled to C:\Onyx\scratch\ghidra\prc2\auditCoreDeposit.txt) sends the cursor item's whole stack once its item ID matches an escrowable currency (0x5adb50, 0x7b0740). Its only gate is the owned-plot check 0x5b41d0; there is no NO TRADE or ownership test, so a stock client sends it.
findings.proposedFix:
Follow whatever Live does:
- refuse deposits of NO TRADE currency into a plot owned outside the depositor's account; and/or
- refuse withdrawals and sale payouts of it to anyone outside the owning account.
Use Live's lines for the refusals.

3. A Trustee on another account withdraws NO TRADE currency the owner deposited.

findings.title: A deleted or renamed character on an access list blocks every later edit
findings.description:
Every non-club name in the submitted list must be a live character, and the client sends the whole list with each edit (permissions.md, 0x3146, every 3 s). A soft-deleted character is renamed '<name>-deleted-<time>'. A renamed character leaves no row under the old name. Either way its stored entry fails the check, the whole edit is refused with no chat line, and the list snaps back (sendCurrent).

The owner can remove the entry. An editor below its group cannot (accessEditRefusal, housingAccessRules.h:86-93), so a Trustee, Co-Owner or guild officer stays locked out until the owner or guild leader notices the cause.
findings.evidence:
- existingCharacterNames filters on deleted_at IS NULL (housingAccess.cpp:53-67).
- Soft delete renames the row (common/database.cpp:377-379); Character:SoftDeletes defaults to true (common/ruletypes.h:180).
- A refused edit only logs and resends the current list (housingAccess.cpp:287-290).
findings.proposedFix: Validate only names that are added or moved (absent from stored.names with that group). A stored name that no longer resolves stays until someone removes it.

findings.title: Coin moved in memory survives a rolled-back act
findings.description:
Since UPK-27, each act changes the character in memory first (AddMoneyToPP, TakeMoneyFromPP, the cursor coin fields, AddAlternateCurrencyValue), saves inside the transaction, then commits. The catch blocks restore nothing.

The commit can fail, or an inner DBcore scope can roll back; the outer commit then rolls back and reports 'an inner transaction rolled back' (common/dbcore.cpp:210-213). One example is giveAndCommit's PutItemInInventory failing in the item layer. The database then returns to the old escrow and purse while memory keeps the change, and the next SaveCurrency writes it:
- a sale or withdrawal pays out and keeps the escrow (a duplicate);
- a purchase, deposit or Add Day loses the payment.
findings.evidence:
- **Memory before commit:** d448a9c0f (UPK-27) moved the money changes ahead of the commit.
- **No restore:** the catch blocks only log and reply (housingSell.cpp:334-343, housingAccount.cpp:372-381, housingPurchase.cpp:186-198).
- **Writes inside the transaction:** AddAlternateCurrencyValue writes memory and calls database.UpdateAltCurrencyValue on the same connection (zone/client.cpp:7343-7347).
- **Untested case:** UPK-27's proof killed the zone mid-transaction; a rollback with the zone still running was not tested.
findings.proposedFix:
Either:
- snapshot the coin fields and alternate-currency values before the act, and restore them in both catch blocks with a money and currency update to the client; or
- write the new purse rows with SQL inside the transaction and copy them into the profile only after commit, as giveAndCommit does for items.
Test by forcing an inner rollback.
findings.worklistOverlap: UPK-27 (done; covers kills, not rollbacks)

findings.title: Two simultaneous guild plot purchases both pass the guild limit
findings.description: The purchase locks only the plot being bought. guildPlotCount is an ordinary read of the transaction's snapshot, which is taken after that one lock. Two officers buying guild plots in two neighborhoods (two zone processes) at the same moment both count 0 and both commit, past Housing:MaxGuildPlotsPerGuild (1). Character limits cannot race this way, because a character's acts run in a single zone process.
findings.evidence:
- lockedProperty locks one row (housingLedger.cpp:58-65).
- countOfType runs a plain SELECT (housingLedger.cpp:327-342).
findings.proposedFix: Lock a per-guild row before counting (SELECT ... FROM guilds WHERE id = <guild> FOR UPDATE), or count with a locking read.

findings.title: A GM's Sell on someone else's plot gives the GM the owner's crate and escrow
findings.evidence:
- housingSell.cpp:187-188 skips the owner checks for a GM.
- :279-281 and :321-326 send the escrow payout to the seller.
- :297-298 sets the crate's owner_character_id to the seller.
- serverPlan.md:449.
findings.proposedFix: Owner decision: either refuse a GM's sale of a plot the GM does not own, or deliver the crate (archived, list C) and the escrow to the plot's owner, as a reclaim does.

findings.title: After a catalog reload, prices and upkeep choices resolve against a catalog the client has not received
findings.description: Since PLC-33 (e0e54e844), a reload updates the server only; clients keep the catalog they received at zone-in. Option keys are positions among the enabled options (housingCatalog.cpp:78-93). An edit that enables, disables or reprices an option (`#realestate cost set`, content flags) therefore makes the client's key point at a different option. A purchase can then charge a currency or amount the window never showed, and an upkeep-option change (account request type 2) can set a currency the player did not pick.
findings.evidence:
- optionAt indexes the server's current options (housingPurchase.cpp:43-49).
- The GM command says players get the new catalog at their next zone-in (housingCommand.cpp:100, :446, :470).
findings.proposedFix:
Either:
- stamp each session with the catalog's load generation, and refuse purchases and upkeep-option changes from an older session with a line telling the player to zone; or
- refuse reloads that change existing options while housing zones hold players.
findings.worklistOverlap: PLC-33 (the no-resend decision this follows from)

findings.title: Unchecked balance read; negative string lengths accepted silently
findings.description:
- **balances():** calls database.QueryDatabase and never checks Success. A failed read sends every record with no balances, so the Manage window shows an empty escrow and 'Expired' instead of the session failing. characterIdentities has the same unchecked call, though it fails loudly further on.
- **WireReader::lengthString:** returns an empty string for a negative length without marking the reader failed, so a malformed field parses on as if it were valid.
findings.evidence:
- housingStore.cpp:32-36 has no Success() test; compare guildOwnsNeighborhood :65, which uses query(), which throws.
- housingWire.cpp:68 has `if (overrun || size <= 0) return {};`.
findings.proposedFix:
- Use query() (which throws) in balances() and characterIdentities().
- Set overrun when the length is negative.

findings.title: Plan text the code no longer follows
findings.description:
1. **Line 139, concurrency:** says each change checks `UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND revision = ?` and a concurrent second change fails cleanly. The code serializes on the property's row lock (lockedProperty, housingLedger.cpp:58-65): the second change waits, then runs on the committed row. Only a transfer offer compares revisions (housingTransfer.cpp:209).
2. **Line 122, event revision:** says events carry the revision after the change. sendEvent writes 0 (housingEvents.cpp:33) and no zone reads it.
3. **Line 129, current property:** says a property change re-sends 0x6fd0 for a current property. refreshClients sends 0x63fd only (housing.cpp:592-596), which merges into the client's record.
4. **Lines 364-365, zone-in order:** list the catalog before pending crates. sendZoneContents delivers pending crates first (housing.cpp:366-385).
5. **flows/escrowAndUpkeep.md:45:** says a deposit first settles, then credits. The plan (serverPlan.md:461), UPK-8's Live numbers and depositInto (housingAccount.cpp:106-115) all credit first, then settle.
findings.evidence: The plan lines and code lines are cited in the description.
findings.proposedFix: Rewrite the five passages to match the code: row locks; revision unused in events; 0x63fd only on a change; pending crates delivered first, or move the delivery after the catalog; deposit credits, then settles.

found.summary:
Audited housingPlacement.cpp, housingPlacementRules.h, the menus, containers, world objects, NPC items, the item tail and the RoF2 housing serialization. I checked them against serverPlan.md, the RoF2 rule sets and Live's item data. The rule sets are 0x5b5ff0, 0x5b69b0, 0x5b6eb0, 0x5b48b0/0x5b45b0 and 0x5b72c0; I disassembled them where the decompile hid the arguments (C:\Onyx\scratch\ghidra\prc2\placementDecomp1.txt, placementDecomp2.txt, placementDisasm2.txt).

Three findings are high:
- B-01: moves between plots skip the client's remove rule, so a Friend can move a neighbour's item to their own plot and take it.
- B-02: storing someone else's stack merges it into the mover's own stack, so the mover becomes its placer.
- B-03: a forged house swap makes a house its own parent and breaks its owner's housing data.

Three are medium:
- B-04: a crate placed in a house is ignored by Pack, Unpack and Move to Crate, and the one-crate limit is checked per destination rather than per plot.
- B-05: Move to Closet picks the highest-id house child, which can be a stored house.
- B-06: Move to Inventory chooses its free slot before the open container returns its contents into that slot.

Five are low (B-07 to B-11).

No defects found in:
- the housing tail and spawn binding serialization;
- world objects (0x1045 updates by GUID, so a move between plots leaves no stale copy);
- NPC spawn and respawn bookkeeping;
- the menus' gates;
- the guards in ContainerTakesItems.

findings.title: Moves between plots skip the client's remove rule
findings.description:
The server judges every row moved to another property with otherPropertyPlacementResult: Move Item on the holder, then Add on the destination. RoF2's 0x5b5ff0 uses its within-plot path only when the source and destination share a plot. Across plots, or when either side has no plot, it first runs the remove rule 0x5b72c0 on the source:
- the placer passes;
- anyone else needs Remove House, Crate or Item (76, 78, 72) for the kind;
- then No Trade (64) applies.
After that it runs the inventory rule set 0x5b69b0 against the destination.

Result: any Friend who owns another plot can move a stored or placed item off plot A onto their own plot B, then pick it up there as B's owner. A default Friend has Add Item and Move Item but not Remove Item, and guild ranks 4-6 are Friends on a guild plot by default.

This works with the unmodified client: Place or Adjust Placement on A's item, then commit inside B. The begin reply's per-region code for B is the server's own other-property verdict, which is 0. A forged 0x5b41 tag-0 record does the same from any zone, because its source may be any property in the session.
findings.proposedFix:
In placementResult, when the row's plot (ancestorOfType plot|guildPlot) differs from the destination's plot, or either has none:
- first return pickUpAccessResult for the source (the record's placer and kind, No Trade, upkeep);
- then return inventoryPlacementResult against the destination.
Keep otherPropertyPlacementResult for moves within one plot.

Unit test: a Friend's commit of plot A's item into plot B is refused with 72.
findings.worklistOverlap: PLC-19 records this cross-plot branch of 0x5b5ff0 as read. Its remaining open points are all about moves within one plot, so this gap is not recorded.

findings.title: Storing another player's stack merges it into the mover's stack
findings.description:
For a move out of a property, both factsFor's stack-merge waiver (:332) and storeInto's merge (:607) look for a destination stack owned by client->CharacterID(). RoF2's between-properties set instead merges into a stack owned by the moved entry's owner; only the inventory set uses the character.

The merged row keeps the target's owner, and the source GUID is retired 'stacked'. The mover becomes the placer of the whole stack, so pickUpAccessResult lets them take it without Remove Item and past No Drop (64).

Scenario: a Friend stores 1 arrow of item X in the shed (Add Item). They then use Move to Shed on the owner's stack of 99 X in the closet, or on a placed stack in the yard. Move to Inventory then gives the Friend all 100.

moveRows has the mismatch inside one function: it merges by row.owner_character_id (:774) but judges the capacity waiver by the mover (:769 via :332). A waived row can therefore be stored as a new entry past the cap.
findings.proposedFix:
Use candidate.row ? candidate.row->owner_character_id : client->CharacterID() as the merge owner in factsFor (:332) and storeInto (:607); moveRows then agrees with its own merge.

Unit test: a Trustee storing another player's stack beside the Trustee's own stack of the same item gets a separate entry owned by the placer.
findings.worklistOverlap: PLC-18 and PLC-28 concern how much of a stack fits a merge, not whose stack it merges into.

findings.title: A forged house swap can make a house its own parent
findings.description:
handleHouseSwap never checks that the stored record is held by the yard. Suppose it names a house stored in the outgoing house's closet; an empty house may be stored there.

The loop over the outgoing house's rows was read before the updates, so it also moves the incoming house's own row:
- updateRow puts the item inside its own property, with placed reset to 0;
- :1413 sets that property's parent_id to itself.

The house disappears from the yard; the client is still told it is placed there (a ghost world object). The property's owner is the plot's owner (set by attachCarried). Every session that loads it fails, because the ancestor walk passes depth 10 and the zone logs 'no housing data is sent'. So someone with Move Item, Remove House and Add House on the yard (a Co-Owner, say) can cut the owner off from all housing data.

A stored house from another plot is also accepted, which is B-01's gap.
findings.evidence:
- Swap Houses is offered only for a stored house whose holder is a plot or guild plot (housingMenus.cpp:120-130); serverPlan.md:581 and MNU-11 describe the swap the same way.
- crateRuleResult refuses only non-empty houses in a closet (housingPlacementRules.h:133-148).
- Session build: housing.cpp:92-106 (ancestry limit), :304-309 (no housing data sent).
findings.proposedFix:
Under the yard's lock, refuse with 1 unless incomingRow->property_id == yard.id.

Unit test: a swap naming a house in the outgoing house's closet is refused and changes nothing.
findings.worklistOverlap: MNU-11 (where Live offers Swap Houses) is related; this gap is not recorded.

findings.title: A crate placed inside a house is never the active crate, and the one-crate limit is checked per destination
findings.description:
placedCrateIn only looks at one property's direct children. So:
- Move to Crate, Pack and Unpack find only a crate placed in the yard. With the crate placed in the house, all three answer 22 'You must have a moving crate placed in your yard or house'. The client finds that crate and keeps those buttons enabled.
- The limit (16) looks only at the destination's own placed crates. A second crate can be placed in the yard while one stands in the house, or the other way round. A house holding a crate can also be placed or swapped onto a plot that already has one.

The client's Place button stays enabled at code 16 and the click sends without re-checking, so the server's rule is the one players get. housingSell.cpp:218-227 finds the sale's crate the same way.
findings.proposedFix:
Write one helper that finds the plot's placed crate across all its descendants, in the client's order (child lists with placed carriers first, PLC-34). Use it for Move to Crate, Pack/Unpack, the sale, and the limit. The limit then refuses a second crate per plot, and a house carrying a crate onto a plot that has one.

Decide whether stored crates count: the client counts any crate property.
findings.liveCheck: Optional: on Live, with a crate stored in the shed, try to place a second crate. This shows whether a stored crate blocks 16 as the client's rule says.

findings.title: Move to Closet stores into the plot's highest-id house, which may be a stored one
findings.description:
When the source isn't a house, the closet becomes the last house or hall child of the plot in id order. A house stored after the placed one has a higher id, because every house stored from inventory gets a new property, as in PLC-7's test on 107 Brimming Way.

Move to Closet from inventory, the shed or the crate then puts the item in the stored house. The Items window's House lists show the placed house's closet, so the item seems to vanish. It can only be reached again by swapping or placing that house.
findings.proposedFix: Resolve the closet as the client's +0x9c does: the plot's placed house or hall, in PLC-34's order, falling back to the first stored one. Share that lookup with handleMoveToStorage's row path.
findings.liveCheck: Optional: on Live, with a placed and a stored house in one yard, Move to Closet an item and see which house lists it.
findings.worklistOverlap: PLC-34 fixed the order the client sees but not the server's closet choice.

findings.title: Move to Inventory picks its free slot before the open container returns its contents
findings.description:
The slot is chosen (:1144) before closeContainersOf (:1147). If the taker has the container open, Object::Close hands its contents back through MoveItemToInventory, which uses the first free general slot: the slot just chosen. The second checkPickUp (:1152) reuses the old slot.

giveAndCommit's PutItemInInventory then deletes the returned item from memory and the client. Its save fails on the unique slot index, so the rollback removes the container too. The pick-up fails with 1, and the returned item disappears from view until the player logs out and back in; it is still saved in the database.

This is a normal action: open your forge, put something in, then pick the forge up. MNU-13 only tested another character picking it up.
findings.proposedFix: Close the container first. Then, inside the transaction, choose the slot after re-reading the candidate: move FindFirstFreeSlotThatFitsItem below closeContainersOf and the re-read, and feed that slot to the final checkPickUp.
findings.worklistOverlap: MNU-13 covered a pick-up by another character only.

findings.title: A request naming an equipment slot places or stores a worn item
findings.description:
inventoryCandidate accepts any possessions location, which includes equipment slots 0-22, as long as the GUID matches. A forged 0x626e, 0x3424 or layout record can place or store an equipped item. takeFromInventory then removes it with RemoveItemFromInventory, which never calls CalcBonuses, so the item's stats stay applied until something else recalculates them.

The client's layout loader uses only non-equipped inventory items (RealEstateItemsWnd.md, How Load plans, step 6).
findings.evidence:
- RoF2ToServerSlot maps possessions slots 0-32 one to one (common/patches/rof2.cpp:7156-7160);
- zone/inventory.cpp:985-997 (no CalcBonuses).
findings.proposedFix: Refuse with 9 unless the slot is a general slot, a general bag slot or the cursor.

findings.title: Store, commit, swap and Mail to Owner act on a source row read before the transaction, without locking its property
findings.description:
These paths read the row before the transaction and lock only the destination (or lock after the read, in Mail to Owner). They then move the item by GUID with ItemLayer::MoveRow, which moves any row that is in play, whoever holds it. The follow-up UPDATE or DELETE on real_estate_items does not check that a row was affected.

A house's items can be handled from both the neighbourhood zone (the Items window's House list) and the interior zone. If another zone picks the item up between the read and the commit, this zone moves the taker's item back into a property with no real_estate_items row. The item is then invisible on the plot and is missing from the taker's inventory after they log back in.

handleMoveToInventory already avoids this by re-reading under the holder's lock (:1148-1152).
findings.proposedFix: In every mutating path, lock the source property and re-read the candidate inside the transaction, as handleMoveToInventory does. Check that the real_estate_items UPDATE/DELETE affected exactly one row.

findings.title: The pick-up limit (33) treats guild halls and houses as different kinds, and reads a carried list that lags behind
findings.description:
Two problems in checkPickUp:
- It compares kindOf(type) == candidate.kind, so a carried non-empty guild hall does not count against picking up a non-empty house, or the other way round. RoF2 compares categories, and halls and houses share category 2.
- The walk starts from the session's carriedIds, which is refreshed only when the propertyChanged event comes back from world. Two quick pick-ups of non-empty houses both pass, because the result is sent before announce.
findings.proposedFix: Compare isHouseKind() on both sides (crate against crate). Start the walk from carriedPropertyIds(database, characterId) read inside the transaction.
findings.worklistOverlap: PLC-6 (done) traced the walk but not the house/hall category match.

findings.title: Two corrections to PLC-19's reading of the within-plot path in 0x5b5ff0
findings.description:
1. The per-item-limit guard calls 0x5b3e90 on the destination's plot, not the destination. A plot is never a crate, so the limit (31) also applies to moves into a crate. The recorded '(not into a crate)' is wrong, and the server's current atItemLimit after the other-property set matches the client. It should not be 'fixed'.
2. The final 24/25 check is on the source property, not the destination: 0x5b6447 tests [arg2+0x40], and arg2 is the source. The server never checks the source's expiry, so it allows moving a stored item out of an expired house that the client refuses with 25.
findings.proposedFix: Correct PLC-19 and RealEstateItemsWnd.md:130. When the within-plot set is aligned, add the source property's expiry (24/25) to it.
findings.worklistOverlap: PLC-19 (open): these points refine its recorded reading.

findings.title: A layout load accepts up to 65,535 records
findings.description: handleLoadLayout runs one transaction per record, each with several reads. A forged 0x5b41 with tens of thousands of tag-0 records (17 bytes each) stalls the zone. The client never sends more records than the yard's, house's and crate's caps allow.
findings.evidence: The u16 count at :1453 is used with no bound beyond the packet length; each record calls storeInto or commitPlacement, which each run viewOf plus the judge.
findings.proposedFix: Refuse a layout whose count exceeds the yard's and house's max_items + max_non_real_estate_items (or a fixed bound), before applying any record.

Decide and record whether a cross-plot move makes the mover the row's placer. The client's inventory set judges the merge waiver by the mover's name, so the server's merge owner must follow the same choice.

Reachable with the unmodified client:

Test: a Friend storing the owner's stack beside the Friend's own stack of the same item gets a separate entry owned by the owner, and the Friend's pick-up of it is refused with 72.

An empty house can be stored in a house's closet: crateRuleResult refuses only non-empty carriers (housingPlacementRules.h:133-137).

With storedPropertyId = the outgoing house H and the record an empty house P in H's closet:

findings.title: A login into a new copy of a house that stands in no yard leaves the character stuck inside
findings.description: Login path: reenterCopy re-creates a copy for any house that still exists and isn't carried. A house stored in its yard's shed, packed into a sale crate, or under a Crate of Eviction is not 'carried', because its item is held by real_estate. The new copy's loadHostedRoot sets rootPlot from yardOf, which is nullopt for such a house. onZoneIn then calls admitOccupant, which falls through to leaveForExitPoint; that throws 'stood in no yard when this copy started' and only logs. /leaverealestate and the front door hit the same throw. After a camp and the copy's discard, every later login repeats this. The likeliest trigger is the reclaim case: an owner camps in their own house, stays away past the 90-day reclaim, and comes back.
findings.evidence: housingInstances.cpp:152 checks only existence and isCarried (housingLedger.cpp:82-90: 'NOT (holder_type <=> real_estate')'); :156-161 template, then runningCopy. housingInteriors.cpp:178-179 rootPlot = yardOf(...); :67-71 a house whose row is unplaced -> nullopt, and a house under a crate has no plot ancestor; :317-319 throw caught at :322; :345-354. housing.cpp:515-523 onZoneIn -> admitOccupant. housingDoors.cpp:85-88 front door. Ways a house leaves its yard while its occupant is offline: housingLedger.cpp:403 (packPlotInto re-parents it under the Crate of Eviction), housingSell.cpp:297, store/swap. INT-26 tested the relog only with the house placed. INT-38 covers only occupants online in a running copy.
findings.proposedFix: World: reenterCopy applies the zone's yard rule (an interior must stand placed on a plot or guild plot) and returns false otherwise, so EQEmu's safe return applies. Zone: leaveForExitPoint with no known yard sends the player to bind with a log line, as arrivedInDiscardedCopy does, instead of throwing. Better: when the stored house's parent is still a plot, use that plot's exit point, which S10 promises for occupants of a stored house. Proof: camp inside a house; from another character store it, then sell the plot (and separately, force a 90-day reclaim); wait past the discard; log in. The character lands at the exit point or at bind, and /leaverealestate works.

findings.title: An item whose upkeep id has no cost (ids 2 and 4) breaks its plot's upkeep; Live charges and stamps nothing
findings.description: upkeepCostItems throws for any placed item whose upkeep id has no enabled cost option. That covers the carved tables (id 2) and the trophies (id 4), which have no cost element in the catalog, as on Live. So once one is placed, world's charge for that plot throws every 10 s. The plot is never charged, never expires and is never reclaimed, and the oldest-first LIMIT 500 retries can starve other plots. The zone's deposit (depositInto -> settleUpkeep) and Add Day/Week (dailyTotal) throw too, so the owner can't fund the plot. stamp() also counts any positive upkeep id as upkeep, so it would stamp and store these items. On Live they stay placed and unstamped through an expiry. The plan says ids 2 and 4 get no element precisely so that they pay nothing.

Catalog costs are 6-24 and 26-35 only (sql/housingCatalog.sql:207-237). serverPlan.md:546 says ids 2 and 4 have no upkeep. Keep the throw for a cost that exists but has no enabled option. The catalog can list the item upkeep ids with no element at load. findings.title: A deposit that leaves the escrow short still clears the expiry and restarts the 90-day reclaim clock
findings.description: depositInto credits, settles, then always clears the stamps; settleUpkeep's escrowFoundEmpty is ignored. A 1-copper deposit into a long-expired plot is entirely eaten by the settle, yet clears the plot's and its houses' stamps. The next charge finds the escrow empty and stamps a new second, and the 90-day reclaim counts from upkeep_expired_time. So anyone can keep an unpaid plot from reclaim with 1 copper every 89 days (deposits are open to everyone, UPK-8), and its house unlocks for up to a charge interval each time. A deposit in a currency the plot doesn't pay upkeep in (escrowCurrencies accepts every catalog currency) clears the stamp the same way. UPK-8 saw Live clear the stamp only on a deposit that covered the accrued time.

UPK-8: 1 pp into a plot expired 1,782 s, settle 43.3125, stamp cleared.

findings.title: Housing:EnableUpkeep off doesn't pause upkeep; the time is billed later
findings.description: With the rule off, processUpkeep returns before any pass, so upkeep_settled_at and next_upkeep_at stay where they were. A deposit or Add Day still runs settleUpkeep, which charges the whole time since the last settle. The first charge after the rule is turned back on bills the entire off period in one lump, which can drain escrows and expire many plots at once. A dormant X3 plot, by contrast, has its clock moved forward so that paused time is never charged. The rule says it charges upkeep on each property's clock, and BLD-4 calls it 'the upkeep clock's own switch'.
findings.evidence: housingUpkeep.cpp:390 early return; :284 the dormant path sets upkeep_settled_at = now and next_upkeep_at. housingLedger.cpp:304 elapsed = now - upkeep_settled_at. housingAccount.cpp:112 settle with no rule check. ruletypes.h:1181. No other EnableUpkeep check exists in the tree.
findings.proposedFix: Make 'off' a pause. World's pass keeps running and handles due plots as it handles dormant ones: settled_at = now, next = now + interval, nothing charged. settleUpkeep charges nothing while the rule is off but still moves upkeep_settled_at. State this in serverPlan.md's rule row. Proof: turn the rule off, wait, deposit and re-enable; nothing is charged for the off period.

findings.title: #realestate poll option silently relabels another poll's option
findings.description: Option labels live in real_estate_poll_labels keyed by the option key alone, and RoF2's 0x6860 is one global key-to-text table. The command writes REPLACE INTO real_estate_poll_labels (id, text) using the option key as the id. Reusing a key in a second poll (key 1 'Yes' after another poll's key 1 'Red') therefore overwrites the first poll's label for every client and in its results, with no warning.
findings.evidence: housingCommand.cpp:416. sql/housingSchema.sql:315-319 (PRIMARY KEY id). polls.md:14 ('the global key -> text table'). housingPolls.cpp:95 reads labels by key across all published polls.
findings.proposedFix: Refuse an option whose key already has a different label (name the poll using it), or have the command allocate a fresh global label id for each option.
findings.worklistOverlap: POL-4, POL-5 (rules only)

verified.evidence: I re-read the code and found no guard. world/housingInstances.cpp:150-161 checks three things only: the property exists, it is not carried, and its template matches. isCarried (common/housingLedger.cpp:82-90) treats any holder_type 'real_estate' as not carried, and that covers a house stored in its shed and a house packed under a crate. The crate's parent_id is 0 in both cases: the reclaim crate at world/housingUpkeep.cpp:188-190 and the sale crate at zone/housing/housingSell.cpp:296-298. In the new copy, loadHostedRoot sets rootPlot = yardOf(...) (housingInteriors.cpp:178-179), which is nullopt here (:63-71). The path is onZoneIn (housing.cpp:515-523) -> admitOccupant (:345 fails) -> leaveForExitPoint, which throws at :317-319 and only logs at :322. /leaverealestate (:328-334) and the front door (housingDoors.cpp:85-88) take the same path. Safe-return rows survive a discard: they are upserted at client_packet.cpp:1862-1871, and Database::DeleteInstance (common/database_instances.cpp:496-510) never deletes them, so every later login repeats this. INT-32 (done) designed reenterCopy's checks with no yard rule, and INT-26 tested only a placed house. S10 (serverPlan.md:581) promises that a stored house's occupants leave by the yard's exit point. Extra case: any #realestate edit raises catalogChanged -> reloadCatalog (housing.cpp:464-477) -> loadHostedRoot, which also resets rootPlot. After that, a running copy of an already-stored house strands anyone who arrives later.
verified.refinedAction: Zone: separate where occupants exit from whether the house stands in a yard. The exit plot is the house's plot ancestor whether its own row is placed or stored (S10), and it must survive a catalog reload. When the house has no plot ancestor (a sale or eviction crate), send the player to bind with a log line, as arrivedInDiscardedCopy does. World (optional): reenterCopy returns false for an interior with no plot ancestor, so no copy of a crated house starts. Proof: a visitor camps inside a hut. (a) Another character stores it; after the 32-minute discard the visitor logs in at the plot's exit point. (b) Sell the plot, and separately force the 90-day reclaim; after the discard the visitor logs in at bind. (c) Run #realestate reload while a stored house's copy is running, then log the camper in: they land at the exit point. /leaverealestate and the front door work in each case.

verified.evidence: The mechanism is right. world/housingUpkeep.cpp:390 is the only check of the rule in the tree (grep). The deposit path still settles (housingAccount.cpp:112), and settleUpkeep (housingLedger.cpp:304) charges all the time since upkeep_settled_at. The rule row (serverPlan.md:155, 'the upkeep clock (D4)') and BLD-4 never say whether off means time is free or billed later. The rule defaults to on, and Peridot never runs with it off.

Either way, zone settles must follow the same rule as world's pass; today a deposit bills while world does not. Write the choice into serverPlan.md:155 and the description at common/ruletypes.h:1181. If pause: world's pass moves due plots' clocks forward as it does for dormant plots, and settleUpkeep charges nothing while the rule is off but still moves upkeep_settled_at.

missedItems.description: Every house standing on a plot at its 90-day reclaim reaches the owner's Crate of Eviction still stamped as expired, and no code clears it there. The plot's expiry stamped the house's property and the house's own record. The reclaim packs both into the crate unchanged, and releasePlot clears only the plot's own stamp. A stamp is cleared only by a deposit, and only for houses placed on the plot being paid. Once the delivered crate is placed on a new plot, the house cannot be moved out, placed or taken home: every placement rule set and the pick-up rule answer 25, and Unpack skips houses. The owner never gets the house or its contents back, which defeats the reclaim's 'send them to the owner'. This is inferred from the code; it has not been run.

Reclaim: :289-303 -> reclaim() :178-200 -> packPlotInto (housingLedger.cpp:385-405) moves the rows with their stamps and re-parents the houses under the crate, while releasePlot (:407-416) clears only the plot. The only other writes that clear a stamp are housingLedger.cpp:316 (placed houses of a plot being paid), :412 (the plot itself) and zone/housing/housingPurchase.cpp:165 (a bought plot). Placement facts take itemUpkeepExpired from the carried house's upkeep_expired_time or the row's upkeep_expired_at (housingPlacement.cpp:335-336), and the inventory, same-property and other-property rule sets all return 25. Pick-up does the same (:890, pickUpAccessResult), and bulk moves skip houses (:765). The crate reaches the owner at a zone-in (housingSell.cpp:105-139). This contradicts UPK-3 (done): 'A house's stamp never outlives its plot's here'. STT-19's reclaim test had one chair and a back-dated plot stamp, so nothing was stamped by a charge, and RCL-5 covers the deleted-owner path, where everything is deleted. Stamped stored stations in the crate are blocked the same way through the record stamp: pick-up has checked it since a971d0a0f (ACC-11), while the open UPK-24 still describes the older behaviour. Live (weak, inferred): master/properties.tsv shows Crates of Eviction (definition 31, e.g. bristle 117747948, 117748371, 117750762) placed on plots with empty child lists, so their contents came out.
missedItems.proposedAction: In world's reclaim, in the same transaction, clear upkeep_expired_time on every property moved under the Crate of Eviction and upkeep_expired_at on every row packed. Those stamps belong to the released plot's expiry. State this in S8 and D7. Proof: on a plot, place a hut holding items and a station. Let the plot expire through a real charge, not a back-dated stamp, then force the 90-day reclaim and take delivery. Place the crate on a funded plot, move the hut out and place it, enter it, and take the station home. missedItems.description: #realestate poll unoption on an option that already has votes breaks the polls for every player. The votes stay, but the label lookup covers only keys still offered. Building the results then throws, after four of the six poll messages have been sent. So no zone ever sends the results or the 'polling available' flag again: not at any zone-in, and not at the refresh the unoption itself triggers. The Vote and Polls windows stop working until the votes are deleted by hand.
missedItems.evidence: unoption deletes only the real_estate_poll_options row (housingCommand.cpp:418-421). labels() collects keys from poll.options only (housingPolls.cpp:78-99). resultsMessage tallies every voted key (:170-178) and calls keyText, which throws for a question poll's key with no label (:114-121). In sendPolls, resultsMessage is the argument of the fifth send (:255), so the throw is caught at :260-262 with OP_PollResults and OP_PollAvailable (0x593a, :258) unsent. pollEdit raises pollsChanged at once (housingCommand.cpp:359). The client needs the lists and the available flag before its vote window opens (polls.md:5, :16). Only GMs can trigger this, and Peridot runs no polls by default (POL-3).
missedItems.proposedAction: Have unoption refuse a key that has votes, or delete its votes in the same transaction. Alternatively, have labels() also look up keys that appear in votes. Proof: vote for an option, unoption it, and zone in: the results list and the Vote window still work, and no 'polls could not be sent' error is logged.
